title: What a Build System Actually Does

questions.question: What is a build system fundamentally doing?
options: Visiting a graph of targets in dependency order, skipping the ones that are up to date
Compiling every source file in alphabetical order
Watching files and recompiling whatever changes
Translating C++ into machine code
questions.explanation: A graph, an order, and a rule for staleness. The compiler does the translating; the build system decides what to translate and when.

questions.question: What is a topological order?
options: One where every target appears after everything it depends on
Alphabetical order of target names
The order the targets were declared in
Smallest targets first
questions.explanation: You cannot link before compiling. The order exists so that whenever a target is reached, everything it needs is already built.

questions.question: A pass over the graph takes no target and some remain. What does that mean?
options: Every remaining target is waiting on another remaining target, which is a cycle
The graph is finished
A target has no inputs
The build is up to date
questions.explanation: No valid order exists, so the build system must refuse and name the targets rather than loop or pick arbitrarily.

questions.question: Which staleness rule is the one people forget?
options: A target is stale when a target it depends on is stale
A target is stale when its output is missing
A target is stale when an input is newer than its output
A target is stale when it has no inputs
questions.explanation: Without it, changing a shared header rebuilds the objects but relinks nothing, and the program is quietly assembled from mismatched pieces.

questions.question: Why does adding a source file sometimes have no effect until you configure again?
options: The graph is worked out at configure time, so building only executes the graph already written down
Because the compiler caches source files
Because timestamps are only read once
Because new files default to being excluded
questions.explanation: Configure decides the graph, build executes it. Editing a file already in the graph is picked up automatically; changing the shape of the graph is not.

questions.question: The build reports that there is no work to do, and you are sure there should be. What is most likely?
options: Nothing the graph knows about changed, so doing nothing is the correct answer
The build system is broken
The output files need deleting first
The compiler is caching results incorrectly
questions.explanation: It is a disagreement about what changed. Either the edit was somewhere the graph does not track, or the graph needs reconfiguring to learn about it.
